purpose: The TUI's priority keys read the queue the way it is read, from HIGH down to a chosen floor, every priority view sits in one key row, and the view the operator built is still there at the next launch.
form:
Three changes to the TUI, no daemon or API change.

1. Floor filter (gh #36). applyFiltersClientSide (tui/internal/ui/model.go:1454), the one filter both local and remote mode use, compares priority by rank (high 3, medium 2, low 1) instead of equality: 1 keeps HIGH, 2 keeps MEDIUM and HIGH, 3 keeps LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH. 'a' (all prioritized) selects exactly what 3 selects, so both keys set the same 'low' state and the separate 'all' value goes; the default view is that state, the same items the default shows today. buildViewStateString (tui/internal/ui/feed.go:14) names the floor: 'Priority: HIGH', 'MEDIUM+', 'LOW+', and keeps 'Hidden: N' for the unprioritized items a floor view leaves out.

2. One priority row (gh #52). 0 keeps today's unprioritized-only view (tui/internal/ui/model.go:658), resolved by evidence: the operator rescues items from it (6 of 24 upvotes) and a floor below LOW would be 76% unscored items. It joins 1/2/3 and 4/* as one key row in the help modal (tui/internal/ui/help_modal.go:170), with i (upvoted) moved beside u and v, the view toggles it belongs with.

3. Persisted view (gh #33). The view is priority, unread/all, archived, upvoted, sort order, source type and kind. It is read once in newModel (tui/internal/ui/model.go:130) from $XDG_STATE_HOME/prismis/tui-view.json (default ~/.local/state/prismis/tui-view.json, resolved like getDefaultDBPath in tui/internal/db/queries.go:318), and written from one place: after Update handles a key, if the view differs from the last one written, it is saved by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the old one, so a crash mid-write never leaves a torn file. A missing file is a first launch and gives the defaults silently; a file that cannot be read or parsed gives the defaults and a status-line message naming the file; a field with an unknown value falls back to that field's default; a kind the data no longer contains falls back to all once the kinds load. A failed save shows a status-line message and never interrupts the session. R resets every field and the reset is saved like any other change.
commitments: Under 1, 2 and 3, the visible items are exactly those at or above the floor, for items of every priority including none, in local and remote mode alike.
The header reads HIGH, MEDIUM+ or LOW+ for the three floors, and 'a' selects the same items as 3.
0 still shows only unprioritized items, and the help modal shows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 as one priority row.
Changing any of the seven view fields and relaunching restores them; R restores and persists the defaults.

A missing view file gives the defaults with no message; an unreadable or corrupt one gives the defaults and a status message naming it; an unknown field value falls back per field; a vanished kind falls back to all.
The view file is written only through a temporary file and rename, at $XDG_STATE_HOME/prismis/tui-view.json or its default.
sacrifices: MEDIUM-only and LOW-only views go away: 2 and 3 now include everything above them, as gh #36 asks.
risk: A persisted view that hides most items (archived on, a narrow kind) greets the next launch with a near-empty list; the header shows every active filter and R resets them, so the state is visible and one key from default.
